en.caption: Knight Destinies
rows: Someone—or something—wronged you in your past. You seek revenge.
You've been promised an inheritance if you can make a name for yourself as a hero.
You're stranded far from home and intend to fight your way back.
A year of solitude gave you clarity and led you down the path of the warrior.
A fortune teller foresaw that you would find your calling in a life of battle.
When the heat of battle takes over, you barely recognize yourself. This scares you.
Friendly (or not-so-friendly) competition with a rival has spurred you to adventure.
You seek a fabled magic weapon or magic suit of armor. You won't rest until you find it.
You feel like a laughingstock but believe you'll make something of yourself on the battlefield.
Someone close to you was kidnapped. You hope to find and rescue them.
You used to be a squire to a brave knight, but that knight died in combat.
Your dreams are haunted by the screams of those you couldn't save in battle.
Unpredictability is a hallmark of your fighting style. You keep enemies on their toes.
Tales of your past heroic deeds might be somewhat exaggerated.
When you lost everything, you realized the only thing you could rely on was your martial skill.
Descended from a family of sorcerers, you were the only one not to show magical aptitude.
You had a near-death experience, and you believe you saw yourself going to the Nine Hells.
You're chasing notoriety, hoping for folk to sing of your deeds for years to come.
You once belonged to a small but mighty militia. Sometimes, you miss the regimented structure of that life.
When monsters attacked your hamlet, you found you had a way with weapons.
You honed your martial skills as a bodyguard to an important political figure.
Slaying monsters is a welcome distraction to the growing emptiness inside you.
en.name: Knight Destinies

en.caption: Telescope Travel Mishaps
rows: The travelers appear adrift in the Astral Sea.
The travelers appear on a different plane of existence, determined randomly or chosen by the DM.

Excess cosmic energy overloads the telescope, causing it to explode. Each creature within 60 feet of the telescope takes {@damage 8d6} necrotic damage. Any Humanoid who survives this damage is transformed into a different kind of creature, as if it had been subject to the {@spell Reincarnate} spell.
A creature from the Astral Sea (such as a {@creature githyanki knight}) appears within 60 feet of the telescope. The DM decides its attitude.
The travelers appear on a different planet or celestial body in the Wildspace system nearest to their target destination.
The travelers arrive at their intended destination, but they each appear coated in harmless slime.

en.caption: Apocalyptic Calamities
rows: The {@creature tarrasque} awakens. (A {@creature kraken}, an {@creature empyrean}, or another titan might also serve as an agent of apocalyptic wrath.)
A deadly plague that's resistant to curative magic sweeps the land.
A prolonged drought leads to terrible famine.
A volcano (or chain of volcanoes) erupts.
A large asteroid crashes into the world.
A vast sinkhole opens, swallowing a city into the Underdark or one of the Lower Planes, or releasing hordes of Fiends.
The gods are stripped of their power and are forced to occupy mortal forms.
The world is drawn into another plane of existence.
The gods war among themselves or against incredibly powerful alien beings.

Magic goes awry, creating random zones of wild magic (where casting any spell of 1st level or higher causes a roll on the {@table Wild Magic Surge|PHB|Wild Magic Surge table} in the {@book Player's Handbook|PHB}) and dead magic (like an {@spell Antimagic Field} spell on a larger scale).
The corpse of a slain god falls to the earth.
Every Dragon is consumed with unthinking rage and unleashes devastation on those living nearby.
en.name: Apocalyptic Calamities

en.caption: Apocalyptic Warnings
rows: A large star or comet appears in the night sky, shedding as much light as the full moon.
A constant stream of meteors is visible in the sky, even during the day, always moving in the same direction.
The sky turns sickly green or bruised purple.
The water of a river or a lake or along a coastline turns to blood, acid, or blue sand.

All creatures born on a particular day (including livestock and wild animals) have a common feature, such as incandescent eyes, a fiery halo, or brightly glowing blood that is visible through the skin.
Locusts, cicadas, wasps, spiders, or snakes swarm in unimaginable numbers.
Earthquakes shake the ground with increasing frequency and strength.
A warning message in countless languages appears all over a city's walls.
A hermit who is a local legend comes to town and delivers a warning.
A dead angel falls from the sky in a fireball that strikes the earth, leaving a charred skeleton with burnt wings and a scorched trumpet.
Everyone has the exact same dream, in which a disembodied presence delivers a warning.
All children simultaneously stop what they're doing and convey the same warning in unison.
en.name: Apocalyptic Warnings

en.caption: Inspiration Cards
rows: When you deal damage to a creature, immediately spend 1 Hit Die to heal yourself. Roll the die, add your Constitution modifier, and regain a number of hit points equal to the total (minimum 1).

As a bonus action, select one creature as your chosen foe. That creature has vulnerability to damage you deal and resistance to all other damage, and it has disadvantage on its attack rolls against any creature other than you. This effect ends when any creature other than you deals damage to the target.

As an action, you are transported to an empty demiplane until the end of your next turn. You can't affect or be affected by anything on the plane you left until you return. You return to the same space you left or, if that space is occupied, to the nearest unoccupied space.
When a creature makes a saving throw, it has disadvantage on that saving throw.
Reroll a single {@dice d20} roll you've just made. You must use the second roll.
When you deal damage to a creature, that creature takes an extra {@dice 1d6} fire damage.
As a reaction, when you take damage, you cause the creature that dealt it to have the {@condition prone} condition.
Take an additional action on your turn.
Take the {@action Disengage} action as a bonus action.
As a bonus action, teleport, with anything you are wearing or carrying, up to 30 feet to a space you can see.
As a reaction, impose disadvantage on the attack roll of a creature you can see.
As a bonus action, regain one expended 1st-level spell slot or a single use of an ability that can be used a certain number of times per day.
Gain advantage on a saving throw.
Gain advantage on an attack roll.
As a bonus action, impose disadvantage on all ability checks of a creature you can see until the end of its next turn.
Take the {@action Help} or {@action Search} action as a bonus action.
As an action, surround yourself with a shroud of death. Until the start of your next turn, any creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of you takes {@dice 1d6} necrotic damage.
Gain advantage on an ability check.
As a reaction, when a creature makes a melee attack that hits you, that creature has the {@condition blinded} condition until the end of your next turn.
As a bonus action, reduce the speed of one creature within 5 feet of you to 0 until the start of your next turn.
As a reaction, when you take damage, the creature that dealt the damage has the {@condition frightened} condition until the end of its next turn. You are the source of its fear.
As a reaction, when you take damage, gain resistance to that damage until the start of your next turn.

en.caption: Villainous Motivations
rows: Eliminate the character and take their place.
Use the character as the key to unlocking immense power, perhaps as a ritual sacrifice.
Claim a treasure from the character, or take the character's wealth and holdings for themself.
Avenge a harm caused by the character or someone the character represents.
Prove their superiority by bringing the character to ruin in a public and inescapable fashion.
Use the character to solve a great mystery and then claim credit.

en.caption: Visions of Ioun
rows: Minotaurs dig beneath the hill and build a temple to Bahamut and other gods.
Minotaurs clad in the garb of a bestial cult summon demons and slay other minotaur priests in a horrific bloodbath.
Monks and knights travel to the hill and construct the abbey at its summit.
Knights defeat a hobgoblin warlord and bring back a {@item Deck of Many Things} and other trophies.
As an army besieges the abbey, a knight draws the Skull card from a {@item Deck of Many Things}. Skull-headed Undead appear and massacre everyone they see.
A huge red dragon emerges from the catacombs beneath the abbey to make his lair atop the hill. Among his treasures is a {@item Deck of Many Things}.
en.name: Visions of Ioun

en.caption: Fated Destinies
rows: You were trained by an organization that opposes a deity or another powerful cosmic force.
You were born under a sign associated with cataclysm, and every attempt to glimpse your future reveals ill omens.
A religious organization imprisoned you, perhaps because of a crime you committed against that faith or because the leaders considered you the servant of a rival power.
You or your family are watched by secretive figures. They usually keep hidden, but you've seen they wear an unknown symbol.
You made a choice in your past that haunts you. Whatever the consequences, it's not clear you made the right choice.
A powerful figure opposed to your beliefs vexes your life; even your triumphs seem to serve this being's ends.
What could have been one of the happiest moments in your life turned into a tragedy.
You inherited land containing the ruins of a temple where a coveted relic was hidden.
You were brought up to believe in a prophecy of impending doom, but you perceive potential and hope where others expect disaster.
An inflexible person with power over you threatened to bring about disaster, but your decisive action prevailed.
The defenders of a religious organization such as a druid circle, paladin order, or temple watch over you.
You are most comfortable at night, and all your greatest successes have taken place then. You also bear a silvery, crescent-shaped birthmark.
Your studies led you to a scrap of prophecy or the memoir of a prominent figure, which calls your beliefs into question.
A devout individual whom you looked up to revealed themself to be false, a disciple of a power opposed to your beliefs.
You were once a favored adherent of a religious order, but you've been cast out in disgrace.
An otherworldly being whispers advice to you in dreams or visitations, taking on different guises and speaking through others.
You were returned to life through resurrection magic, divine intervention, or a mysterious circumstance you don't yet understand.
When you adopted your current beliefs, your life changed dramatically for the better.
While you never placed much stock in the beliefs you were taught, adhering to them saved you from a catastrophe.
You have a well-used holy symbol from someone you looked up to, and you feel uncertain anytime you're without it.
You were born to a family of divinely favored folk, and they have big expectations for you.
Your soul, or a loved one's, is doomed to be taken by a Fiend, a powerful Undead, or another wicked power.
